body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo sets a new milestone for the global industry by integrating and linking key technologies across advanced sectors, including future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Showcasing Daegu Metropolitan City’s accumulated industrial cultivation capabilities, leading domestic and international tech enterprises and innovative startups will assemble to present field-validated technologies and products designed to lead future markets. Alongside the main exhibition, international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation programs will run concurrently, elevating the event into Asia’s premier global tech business platform.

Participating as an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, ChinaByte (比特网) is China’s first specialized technology media outlet and ICT news organization, established in 1997. Over three decades, ChinaByte has chronicled and influenced the rapid transformation of China’s IT sector, setting numerous industrial milestones including publishing the first online advertisement in Chinese internet history. Today, ChinaByte delivers in-depth analysis and prompt reporting spanning enterprise ICT, AI, robotics, semiconductors, and smart mobility, cementing its reputation as a trusted business media source for C-level executives, technical leaders, and IT professionals across China. Having evaluated the commercial viability of emerging technologies from the perspective of the real economy and industrial supply chains, ChinaByte returns to Daegu two years after covering FIX 2024, serving as a vital bridge connecting promising South Korean tech companies with Asian and Chinese markets. An advance interview was conducted with Stephanie Chen (Chen Dongfang), Editor-in-Chief of ChinaByte, to discuss Korea-China cooperation in the era of embodied intelligence and her expectations for FIX 2026.
Q1. Could you introduce your media to the Korean audience?

ChinaByte is one of China’s leading ICT media, established in early 1997 — among the very first professional technology media in the country. Over nearly three decades, ChinaByte has witnessed and influenced the development of China’s IT industry and created numerous milestones in the history of the Chinese Internet, including carrying what is widely recognized as China’s first Internet advertisement.

Today, ChinaByte serves a high-end business community with comprehensive, professional and up-to-date news reports and viewpoints, keeping pace with industry trends across enterprise ICT, AI, robotics, semiconductors and smart mobility. It has become the preferred website for C-level executives, technical decision-makers, business decision-makers and IT professionals in China.
Q2. What are your views on recent trends in industrial technology, mobility and AI?

We witness deep integration of industrial technology, mobility and AI, with embodied intelligence as the key bridge connecting digital intelligence and the physical world. Industrially, large models and digital twins are being deployed more quickly, driving smart manufacturing from partial upgrades to full-line collaboration. In mobility, intelligent vehicles and low-altitude transport expand boundaries, where hardware-software integration defines core competitiveness. Embodied intelligence is moving from lab demos to limited B-side rollout, prioritizing industrial inspection, flexible assembly and logistics. Chinese supply chains tackle bottlenecks like dexterous hands, servo joints and vision-language-action models, gathering physical interaction data to lower hardware costs. As an enabling foundation, AI balances industrial application and compliance. Domestic innovation stays pragmatic for real economy needs. Household adoption remains distant; limited generalization and the absence of standards slow commercialization, which will advance step by step.

body.x: Q3. Which FIX 2026 topics will your audience be most interested in?
Based on the interests of ChinaByte’s readers — CIOs, CTOs and business decision-makers — we see six themes generating the strongest attention:

1. Humanoid robots and embodied AI — readers are keenly interested in Korea’s humanoid ecosystem (teams like AeiROBOT that stood out at FIX 2025), including core components such as reducers, screws and dexterous hands, and real-world deployment scenarios.
2.UAM/eVTOL commercialization pathways — both China and Korea have ambitious low-altitude economy policies; Korea’s K-UAM program and the Daegu testbed are reference models for our readers.
3. Next-generation batteries and semiconductors — solid-state batteries and AI chips (HBM, edge AI) are areas where the Chinese and Korean supply chains are highly complementary.
4. Korea’s startup ecosystem and global matching — the Plug and Play Korea Expo and Startup Arena IR pitches are a valuable pipeline for Chinese investors and industrial partners.

5. FIX Innovation Awards winners — the FIX awards are becoming a leading indicator of Asian innovation; we will highlight the winners’ technologies and their potential for cooperation with Chinese partners.
Q4. How was your media’s participation in FIX 2024, and what are your expectations for this year’s edition?

FIX 2024 was a landmark edition — the first year the ITCE and ROBEX expos were merged into a single platform. Our reporting team was deeply impressed by several moments on the show floor: the crowds gathered around the Tesla Cybertruck’s first close-up showcase at a Korean regional expo; Hyundai’s SPACE Mobility concept car and Mobion (which debuted at CES 2024), showcasing the imagination of software-defined vehicles; and the Korean debut of ARTEMIS, the bipedal robot from UCLA’s RoMeLa lab. Our coverage of the show garnered 68,000 reads and confirmed one thing for us: FIX is not just another regional expo — it is one of the best windows into Korean and Asian innovation.

For FIX 2026, we have three expectations. First, further internationalization — we hope to see an even stronger global network of media partners and a buyer-matching program. Second, deeper AI themes — moving from the “All on AI” slogan toward concrete technology layers: AI infrastructure, embodied AI, and AI semiconductors. Third, more substantive China–Korea industry matching — we hope to see more procurement talks, joint R&D and supply-chain partnerships being formed right on the EXCO show floor.

body.x: Q5. As FIX’s official global media award partner, how do you see your media’s role?
We deeply treasure our role as an official global media award partner of FIX — and we see it as a professional responsibility, not merely an honorific.

As a partner media on the jury side, ChinaByte will evaluate entries through the lens of the Chinese industry, focusing on technologies with commercial clarity, supply-chain value and China–Korea partnership potential: Can it be mass-produced? How steep is the cost curve? Does it solve real-world pain points? Is there complementary capacity and market demand in China? At the same time, drawing on our long-standing professional coverage of China’s IT industry, we will bring the award-winning companies and their technology stories — accurately and in depth — to China’s CIOs, CTOs and industrial investors, helping the FIX Innovation Awards build credibility in China.
We look forward to watching the awards grow into “Asia’s CES Award,” and ChinaByte is committed to being its chronicler and champion in China.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
